name: Affordability Crisis
title: Tip And Overtime Deductions Won’t Solve America’s Affordability Crisis | Aparna Mathur
description:
In my latest TaxVox piece, I argue that while the new deductions for tip income and overtime pay are politically popular, they are unlikely to make a meaningful difference for most working families. Here are my key takeaways using Urban-Brookings Tax Policy Center modeling:
• The benefits are limited. Most workers don't receive substantial tip income or overtime pay.
• The tax savings are modest. Income limits, dollar caps, and other restrictions mean many eligible workers receive relatively small benefits.
• They don't address the real drivers of affordability. Housing, childcare, and healthcare costs remain the biggest pressures on family budgets.
So where could these billions of dollars have a bigger impact?
• Expand the Earned Income Tax Credit to boost after-tax incomes for millions of low- and moderate-income workers.
• Invest in AI upskilling and workforce training to help workers adapt to a changing economy and access better-paying jobs.
If our goal is to improve affordability, we should focus on policies that deliver broader and more lasting benefits.
